findings.title: Storage update failures are recorded as legacy failures
findings.body: This branch returns immediately when `Storage.Update` fails, but records the failure with `recordLegacyDuration` even though no legacy call was made. This misattributes unified-storage failures in dual-writer metrics, making operational monitoring of the new mode unreliable; record the storage duration instead.

findings.title: Delete-collection legacy result is recorded as storage latency
findings.body: The goroutine measures the legacy delete-collection call, but records it with `recordStorageDuration`. Legacy failures and latency are therefore reported as storage metrics, while legacy metrics omit them. Use the legacy duration recorder here.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses the object name as the kind
findings.body: On successful deletes, this passes `name` where the other paths pass `options.Kind`. The delete duration metric is consequently labeled with each object's name rather than its resource kind, producing incorrect labels and potentially unbounded metric cardinality. Pass the kind instead.

findings.title: Async legacy writes replay the original update input after storage has committed
findings.body: The goroutine calls `Legacy.Update` with the original `objInfo` after `Storage.Update` has already executed it. If `objInfo.UpdatedObject` is stateful or derives its result from the old object/resource version, this second invocation may produce a different update or fail; even ordinary concurrent updates can make the legacy write apply stale data. The previous implementation wrapped the already-computed unified object for legacy. Capture and replicate the committed object (and equivalent create/delete state) rather than re-executing a request against potentially changed state.

findings.title: Background legacy writes can outlive shutdown
findings.body: Each write launches an untracked goroutine, and `Destroy` immediately destroys both backends without waiting for in-flight legacy writes. A request can return, shutdown can close the legacy storage, and the goroutine can then fail or race against teardown, leaving the safety-copy write unapplied. Track and drain outstanding writes before destroying the legacy backend, or otherwise provide a lifecycle-safe worker.
